name: cron_dump
description: Inventory the scheduling candidates of an extracted Linux root, with what it looked in, what it did not, and what it could not read: /etc/crontab, /etc/cron.d, the cron.hourly to monthly directories (with each script's mode), the per-user spools, and systemd timers in the system and user unit directories and in each account's ~/.config/systemd/user and ~/.local/share/systemd/user (the homes etc/passwd lists, and every directory under home/ and root, so an account that was deleted still has its home looked in). A cron or timer file over 64 MiB is named, not read whole. A cron line keeps its physical line number, the schedule, the user (a table's user field, or a spool file's name) and the command as the exact substring of the line; a timer keeps every assignment in the file in order with its section and line, the empty ones included, plus a naive reading (first schedule, last Unit=) that says it applies no reset, drop-in or override. It is a candidate inventory and not every scheduling mechanism: at jobs, anacron, .service units' ExecStart, generator output and runtime units are not read (named in `unsupported`), systemd drop-ins are listed and not merged, links (aliases, masks, enablement) are listed and not followed, and a listed job is not evidence that it ran. Coverage (read errors, walk errors, links, pipes and devices that were never opened) is computed before `contains` filters anything, so a filtered-out error still shows; a cron line that matches no table shape is counted and located. A file's modification time is a lead to explain, not a conclusion. SENSITIVE: a cron command, an environment value and a unit's Environment= can hold a secret; the answer carries the schedule, user, locators, the command's length and the environment variables' names, and never the command, the values or the raw line. write_text: true (refused outside a job) creates $OUT/cron-text.jsonl, mode 0600; preview_text: true (refused outside a job) puts a cron command in the answer; run it as a job with secret_output: true.

root.description: The root of an extracted file system (a link is refused; links inside it are listed and not followed)

contains.description: Case-insensitive regex over the command, the unit and the script path; it filters what is returned, never what is counted as looked at

limit.description: Entries and unparsed lines shown inline (default 200 each); all are counted and, when there are more, the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in pages.<list>.all_results

write_text.description: Write the raw line, the command and the environment of each cron entry, and each timer's complete assignments, to $OUT/cron-text.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; a file already there is refused

preview_text.description: Put each cron entry's raw line, command and environment values in the answer (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true
